newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends lower on CBOT wheat, Egypt talk.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends lower on CBOT wheat, Egypt talk.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended lower in a late sell-off as CBOT wheat dropped on heavy fund-selling and on talk that Egypt may have rejected a cargo of U.S. wheat, traders said.

"Fund selling in Chicago triggered some stops and that got the ball rolling," a trader said. "People are pointing to this Egyptian rumor to explain why the funds were selling, but we'll have to wait and see."
Wheat had been up at the midsession on spillover strength from CBOT soybeans, which gained on foreecasts for freezing weather Wednesday and Thursday in the northern Midwest states.
But agronomists said corn and soybeans may be little-harmed by a freeze, which knocked soy and corn futures lower late in the session.
KCBT wheat closed one to 6-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with Dec down 6-1/4 cents at $4.32-1/4. Dec had seen an intraday high of $4.43-1/2.

Traders said Prudential and FIMAT each sold one million Dec. FIMAT also bear-spread 1.5 million March/Dec at 10-1/2 to 13 cents. LFG sold one million March and 700,000 Dec. Refco bull-spread one million Dec/March. Continental bought two million Dec and CIS bought 1.5 million July, traders said.
KCBT estimated Wednesday's wheat futures volume at 31.365 million bushels, compared to 24.545 million Tuesday
